![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/d486581ea48bc96adc1269fbf40d1d71a547e92977f71e3a74336a147ef9b222.png)

A potato $P$ is fired from a cannon $C$ at an angle of $\frac{\pi }{6}$ radians from the horizontal. The horizontal distance the projectile travels increases at a rate of $18\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$ If the angle of elevation does not change, what is the speed of the potato?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/8b5af04f58fe65b46adaae47d97b857d1e8765122a811179cf25ba22733e6415.png)

Let $x$ be the horizontal distance from the potato to the cannon and $z$ be the actual distance between them, as shown above.

We want to find $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.$ To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $z.$ Relative to the angle $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ the sides $x$ and $z$ are the adjacent and hypotenuse, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{x}{z} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{x}{z} \\ z & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(z) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}x) \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=18\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\cdot 18=12\sqrt{3}.
$$

Therefore, the speed of the potato is $12\sqrt{3}\,\text{m/s}.$
